title.en: AN ACT FOR THE REORGANIZATION OF THE MINING BUREAU OF THE PHILIPPINE ISLANDS.

text.en:
Until otherwise provided by law, the employees of the Mining Bureau shall be:
(a) An officer in charge, detailed by the Military Governor from the Army of the United States and
drawing no salary.
(b) A chief clerk, interpreter and stenographer, at one hundred and twenty-five dollars per month.
(c) A mining engineer and assayer, at one hundred and twenty-five dollars per month.
(d) A record clerk, at twenty-seven dollars and fifty cents per month.
(e) An engineer's helper and assistant record clerk, at twelve dollars and fifty cents per month.
(f) A janitor, at seven dollars and fifty cents per month.
(g) A laborer, at five dollars per month.

In this Act whenever a sum of money is mentioned it shall be understood to refer to the money of
the United States.

This Act shall take effect on its passage.
Enacted, October 10, 1900.
